title: "Machito Goes to Memphis" released as Dr. King died
summary: The RCA album's release coincided with Martin Luther King's assassination, so nobody wanted a Memphis theme; it later sold abroad.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: I see, okay. There's an album better than that one you did for Cotique. You did two years before that, when Martin Luther King had died, "Machito goes to Memphis". There was no promotion on that at all, Macho.

Yes. We was so lucky, because when that album start to, they start o spread out for the exhibition, the late Martin Luther King got killed and as mentioned, "Machito comes from Memphis", nobody want to know about Memphis. The people they was so ashamed. They lose a great guy like Martin Luther King, that he mean so well, that both groups they don't want to hear about Memphis, really. So now "Machito goes Memphis" so it wasn't called for for that particular time.
Uh-huh, but yet most of these albums finally went to other countries and they become best sellers there.
